AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: To determine if home blood pressure measurement (HBPM) provides comparable results to clinic blood pressure (BP) measurement.

AbstractText.Label: STUDY DESIGN
AbstractText.content: A prospective, single-centre study of 37 pregnant and early post-partum women with a hypertensive pregnancy or at high-risk of developing a hypertensive pregnancy were asked to perform HBPM for a minimum period of one week. This was subsequently compared to clinic BP measurement both before and after the period of home measurement.

AbstractText.Label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
AbstractText.content: The accuracy of HBPM compared to clinic measurement, and the acceptability by patients for HBPM.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The HBPM was comparable to clinic measurements [for the systolic blood pressure (SBP), the mean home reading was 123.4mmHg (122.0-124.9mmHg) versus 123.9mmHg (121.3-126.5mmHg) for the clinic reading (p=0.69); for the diastolic blood pressure (DBP) the mean home reading was 81.6mmHg (80.4-82.8mmHg) versus 84.4mmHg (82.6-86.2mmHg) for the clinic (p<0.01)]. There were no reported issues associated with the use of HBPM, but it did lead to 5 women contacting health care professionals for management of their BP between clinic visits.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: HBPM provides comparable results to the clinic BP measurement. It is also an acceptable technique for pregnant and early post-partum women. However, it should be used as an adjunct to clinic measurement, and cannot at this present stage replace clinic visits or clinic BP measurement.
